The *Loka Sutta* (Ud 3.10; PTS Ud 32) is the tenth and final discourse of the *Nandavagga*, the third chapter of the *Udāna* in the Khuddaka Nikāya. Set shortly after his awakening, the sutta depicts the Buddha contemplating the nature of the world and future rebirth.

The text is extensively cited and paralleled across early Buddhist and paracanonical literature.

No retrieved secondary literature passages discuss Ud 3.10 directly; academic references to a *Loka Sutta* or *Paloka Sutta* typically concern homonymous discourses in the *Itivuttaka* (Iti 112 / AN 4.23) or the *Saṁyutta Nikāya* (SN 12.44, SN 35.82).
